subject: Medicine
concept: Safe transfusion requires appropriate indication, correct patient identification, compatibility testing, correct administration and monitoring.

content.definition: Safe transfusion requires appropriate indication, correct patient identification, compatibility testing, correct administration and monitoring.
content.explanation: Transfusion safety includes patient identification, sample labeling, ABO/Rh compatibility, antibody screening and crossmatching as appropriate, bedside verification and monitoring. Reactions may be immune or non-immune and acute or delayed.
content.mechanism: Transfusion safety includes patient identification, sample labeling, ABO/Rh compatibility, antibody screening and crossmatching as appropriate, bedside verification and monitoring. Reactions may be immune or non-immune and acute or delayed.
content.clinical_relevance: ABO-incompatible transfusion can cause severe acute hemolysis. Suspected transfusion reaction requires immediate assessment and transfusion-service involvement. Transfusion should be used when expected benefits outweigh risks.
content.diagnosis: Diagnosis uses the appropriate clinical, laboratory, microbiologic, marrow or blood-bank studies for the suspected condition.
content.treatment: Management is disease- and patient-specific and should follow current authoritative guidance.
